name: Question 5
problem:
Consider the following relation defined on the set $A=\{\alpha ,\beta ,\delta \}.$ 

$$
R=\{(\alpha ,\alpha ),(\beta ,\beta ),(\beta ,\alpha ),(\delta ,\alpha ),(\delta ,\beta )\}
$$

Select the options that make the following reasoning correct:

In this relation, for all $x,y,z\in A,$ we have

$$
(x,y){{field-1}}R\,\text{and}\,(y,z){{field-2}}R\,⟹\,{{field-3}}\in R.
$$

Therefore, the relation is 
{{field-4}}.

For example, since $(\delta ,\beta )$ and $(\beta ,\alpha )$ belong to $R,$ transitivity of $R$ requires 
{{field-5}}
$\in R.$
worked_solution:
A binary relation $R$ defined on a set $A$ is *transitive* if, for all $x,y,z\in A,$ we have

$$
(x,y)\in R\,\text{and}\,(y,z)\in R\,⟹\,(x,z)\in R.
$$

In other words, if the pairs $(x,y)$ and $(y,z)$ belong to a transitive relation, then the pair $(x,z)$ should also be in the relation.

It's sufficient to check all the "linked" pairs of the form $(x,y)$ with $x\ne y$ and $(y,z)$ with $y\ne z:$

- Consider the pair $(\beta ,\alpha )$ whose second component is $\alpha .$ It can't be linked with any pair from $R$ since none of them have a first component of $\alpha $ and a second component other than $\alpha .$

- Consider the pair $(\delta ,\alpha )$ whose second component is $\alpha .$ It can't be linked with any pair from $R$ since none of them have a first component of $\alpha $ and a second component other than $\alpha .$

- Consider the pair $(\delta ,\beta )$ whose second component is $\beta .$ It can be linked with the following pair from $R$ whose first component is $\beta :$ 

- Linking $(\delta ,\beta )$ with $(\beta ,\alpha )$ requires that $(\delta ,\alpha )\in R,$ and this pair is in $R.$ $\,\,✓$

So, for all $x,y,z\in A,$ we have

$$
(x,y)\in R\,\text{and}\,(y,z)\in R\,⟹\,(x,z)\in R.
$$

Therefore, the relation is $\text{transitive}.$

EXPLANATION

A binary relation R defined on a set A is transitive if, for all x,y,z∈A, we have (x,y)∈Rand(y,z)∈R⟹(x,z)∈R. In other words, if the pairs (x,y) and (y,z) belong to a transitive relation, then the pair (x,z) should also be in the relation.

It's sufficient to check all the "linked" pairs of the form (x,y) with x≠y and (y,z) with y≠z:

  • Consider the pair (β,α) whose second component is α. It can't be linked with any pair from R since none of them have a first component of α and a second component other than α.

  • Consider the pair (δ,α) whose second component is α. It can't be linked with any pair from R since none of them have a first component of α and a second component other than α.

  • Consider the pair (δ,β) whose second component is β. It can be linked with the following pair from R whose first component is β:

    • Linking (δ,β) with (β,α) requires that (δ,α)∈R, and this pair is in R. ✓

So, for all x,y,z∈A, we have (x,y)∈Rand(y,z)∈R⟹(x,z)∈R.

Therefore, the relation is transitive.
